title_lines: THE SADDLER'S WORKSHOP 🐒🪑 A chair cups you from all sides.
A horse-saddle dips two ways. But a MONKEY needs three dips —
two legs and a tail! And here, the professor's test falls silent… 🎧
question: Which sound is the monkey's saddle — THREE ridges up, THREE valleys down? 🐒
hint_lines: Count the high sides around the circle! A pit has none, a peak has none
(everything falls) — a horse-saddle rises in TWO facing directions.
The monkey saddle rises in THREE, and falls in the three between. 💡

options.label: A
options.explain: That chair cups you from EVERY side — a minimum, no high sides at all. The second-derivative test could have told you that one all by itself! 🙂

options.label: C
options.explain: The HORSE-saddle! Two ups facing each other, two downs between. Count again — the monkey needs one more of each. 🙂

options.label: D
options.explain: A peak — every side falls away below you. A maximum, and no seat for a monkey at all. 🙂

success_text: THREE AND THREE! 🐒🎉 Up–down–up–down–up–down around one circle. Here the Hessian is all zeros and the second-derivative test goes silent — but your ear classified the point anyway. Where algebra shrugs, music speaks.
